papers.abstract_zh: 背景:毛细支气管炎是一种常见的病毒性下呼吸道感染,主要影响2岁以下儿童,在英国由呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒,RSV)引起的病例高达80%。诊断主要表现为临床症状,儿童通常出现流涕症状,随后发展为咳嗽、进食困难和发热。NICE建议将支持性治疗作为治疗的主要治疗方式,并不推荐常规使用抗生素、类固醇、吸入性支气管扩张剂和胸部X光检查,但临床实践中仍存在对这些建议的不遵守现象。在较大儿童中,诊断的确定性进一步降低,RSV阳性本身并不能确认毛细支气管炎,这在缺乏年龄特异性指导的群体中,造成了临床和抗菌药物使用管理的挑战。NICE建议在这一年龄组中考虑其他诊断,包括病毒性诱发喘息或早发性哮喘,特别是在存在反复喘息、无湿啰音或个人或家族过敏史的情况下。本次审计旨在评估年龄超过2岁的RSV阳性儿童是否接受了支持性治疗,并在开具抗生素的情况下,确定与抗生素处方相关的临床因素。方法:在英国皇家德文郡和埃克塞特医院进行了一项单中心回顾性审计。通过EPIC电子病历系统,共识别出83名年龄超过2岁且RSV阳性的儿科患者,这些患者于2024年10月至2025年2月期间就诊于儿科部门。提取了有关人口统计学、危险因素、临床表现、检查、治疗和结果的数据。结果:44.6%的年龄超过2岁的RSV阳性儿童接受了抗生素治疗,尽管NICE建议将支持性治疗作为治疗的主要方法。45.8%的患者需要住院治疗。发热(64.9%)、呼吸窘迫(59.5%)和胸部X光检查结果是与抗生素处方最显著相关的临床发现。值得注意的是,51.4%的接受抗生素治疗的患者进行了胸部X光检查,尽管NICE并未推荐常规进行此类检查,其中94.7%的检查结果异常。这些发现已被广泛认为是模拟肺炎而非确诊肺炎,不应用于指导疑似毛细支气管炎的抗生素处方。关键的是,70.3%的接受抗生素治疗的患者未进行血液检查,这意味着大多数处方是在没有任何支持性炎症标志物的情况下开具的。62.1%的抗生素处方是由Tier 1临床医生开具的。此外,还存在更广泛的指南不遵守现象,42.2%的患者接受了吸入器或雾化器治疗,31.3%的患者接受了类固醇治疗,而NICE并未推荐在毛细支气管炎中常规使用这些药物。结论:本次审计揭示了年龄超过2岁的RSV阳性儿童管理中存在显著的指南不遵守现象,近一半的患者接受了抗生素治疗,其中许多患者缺乏细菌感染的客观证据。在这一年龄组中,由于毛细支气管炎、病毒性诱发喘息和早发性哮喘的重叠,诊断的不确定性是主要驱动因素,但无法单独解释观察到的广泛不遵守现象。本次审计得出的关键建议如下。建议对Tier 1临床医生进行针对性教育,以提高对差异性诊断、抗菌药物管理以及在这一年龄组中适当使用检查的认识。抗生素处方应有明确的临床依据记录,并且未来审计周期中需要改善对过敏史、吸烟暴露和体检结果的记录。这些发现突显了儿科抗菌药物管理中的更广泛挑战:在缺乏针对性教育和明确本地指导的情况下,诊断的不确定性可能导致抗生素的过度使用,而这一人群的证据基础仍然有限。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估两年内 RSV 阳性儿童的管理,解决诊断 毛细支气管炎 时临床不确定性的挑战,以及持续不遵守 NICE 指南建议支持性护理而非常规抗生素使用的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 英国皇家德文郡和埃克塞特医院进行了一项单中心回顾性审核,涉及 83 名年龄超过 2 岁、RSV 检测呈阳性并于 2024 年 10 月至 2025 年 2 月期间到儿科就诊的患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 提取了有关人口统计、风险因素、临床表现、调查、管理和结果的数据,重点关注抗生素处方实践和相关临床因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: 尽管 NICE 指南建议支持性护理,但 44.6% 的两岁以上 RSV 阳性儿童仍服用了抗生素。此外,45.8%的患者需要住院,51.4%的患者进行了胸部X光检查,其中94.7%的患者显示异常。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 审计强调,在两年多的时间里,在管理 RSV 阳性儿童方面,严重不遵守 NICE 指南,许多抗生素处方缺乏细菌感染的客观证据。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了临床医生需要进行有针对性的抗菌药物管理教育,以及对 RSV 阳性儿童进行准确的 诊断 以减少不必要的抗生素使用的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单中心回顾性审核,可能会影响普适性。证据是中等的,因为它是基于观察数据而不是实验或前瞻性研究。

papers.title: AN AUDIT OF UNNECESSARY CHEST X-RAY USE IN CHILDREN UNDER 2 YEARS WITH BRONCHIOLITIS IN A DISTRICT GENERAL HOSPITAL PAEDIATRIC EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
papers.abstract: Background: Bronchiolitis is a common lower respiratory tract infection most commonly due to RSV with peak incidence in infants less than a year old, 1.5-2 times more common in boys than girls. It is typically self-limiting and requires solely supportive management, however, in some cases, acute complications such as bacterial infection, respiratory distress, hypoxia and apnoea may occur, requiring admission or medical management. Sequelae can also arise such as recurrent wheeze and asthma. Less experienced or informed health professionals may be tempted to investigate and manage like adults, and this can lead to the over-use of chest x-rays in children and avoidable exposure to radiation. The National Institute of Clinical Excellence (NICE) in England have published guidelines in bronchiolitis management however adherence is lacking. “Do not routinely perform a chest x-ray in children with bronchiolitis.” - NICE. Methods: Retrospective clinical audit of infants aged 0-24 months who presented to Paediatric Emergency Department at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary A&E between January 2026 and April 2026 in first presentation of illness with a clinical diagnosis of bronchiolitis were included. 130 out of 171 met the criteria. Exclusion criteria included those with supplemental oxygen requirements, severe respiratory distress, significant comorbidity such as chronic lung disease, immunodeficiency, neuromuscular disorders, congenital heart disease and previous CXR for the same illness within 2 weeks. Assessing those who received CXR and why, who reviewed, whether they were admitted and clinical uncertainty. Results: 16 out of 130 ( 12.3%) of patients received chest x-rays, 12 out of 130 ( 9.2%) were admitted. Of those who received chest x-rays,11 out of 16 ( 68.8% ) had no justifiable reason as per criteria set out by NICE guidelines. There was diagnostic uncertainty in 20% of cases. First assessor level was resident doctor in 81.4% of cases. Of the chest x-rays performed, 75% were reported normal. 81.8% of unjustified chest x-rays were reported as normal, meanwhile 60% of justified CXR’s were normal. Two abnormalities noted within the unjustified category: 1. Bilateral mild peri bronchial wall thickening. Otherwise, No focal lung lesions. Small ill-defined right paracardial patchy opacity could suggest early infective process. Otherwise, no focal lung lesions. Two abnormalities noted within the justified category: 1. Right retrocardiac and Right lower zonal increased opacification silhouetting Right hemidiaphragm likely infective. Mild peri-bronchial cuffing suggesting small airways inflammation. There was a strong positive correlation between those who received CXR and those who were admitted φ = 0.528, p=0.0000031. A statistically significant moderate correlation existed between those who received a CXR and diagnostic uncertainty p=0.0006 . While first assessor was commonly resident, there was no statistical correlation (p=0.1915). See Reason for CXR table (Table 1). Conclusions: 87.7% did not receive chest x-rays. Which reflects sound clinical judgment in the majority of cases, but this is below the 100% target. Some potential reasons may be clinical uncertainty, in which case a CXR can help differentiate. This audit revealed level of confidence was more likely the reason for CXR request than assessor level.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the unnecessary use of chest x-rays in children under 2 years with bronchiolitis, specifically examining the frequency of chest x-ray use, reasons for its use, and the correlation with admission and diagnostic uncertainty. The central question is whether chest x-rays are appropriately used in this pediatric population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a retrospective clinical audit of infants aged 0-24 months who presented to the Paediatric Emergency Department at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary A&E between January 2026 and April 2026. The audit included patients with a clinical diagnosis of bronchiolitis, excluding those with supplemental oxygen requirements, severe respiratory distress, significant comorbidity, or previous CXR within 2 weeks. The methods involved assessing the reasons for chest x-ray requests, assessor levels, admission status, and diagnostic uncertainty.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The audit found that 12.3% of patients received chest x-rays, with 68.8% of these having no justifiable reason according to NICE guidelines. Additionally, 75% of chest x-rays were reported as normal, and there was a strong positive correlation between chest x-ray use and admission (φ = 0.528, p=0.0000031). The level of confidence was more likely the reason for chest x-ray requests than the assessor level.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There was a statistically significant moderate correlation between chest x-ray use and diagnostic uncertainty (p=0.0006). However, the review does not provide detailed information on the specific diagnostic uncertainties or the impact of these uncertainties on clinical decision-making. The study also does not explore the potential consequences of unnecessary chest x-ray use in terms of radiation exposure or cost-effectiveness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The audit highlights the need for improved adherence to NICE guidelines to reduce unnecessary chest x-ray use in children with bronchiolitis. It suggests that further research should focus on understanding the reasons for diagnostic uncertainty and developing strategies to improve clinical judgment in such cases. Additionally, there is a need for better education and training for health professionals to ensure appropriate use of imaging in this population.

analysis.summary_en: This review presents a clinical audit of chest x-ray use in children under 2 years with bronchiolitis, conducted at a district general hospital. The study found that 12.3% of patients received chest x-rays, with 68.8% of these being unjustified according to NICE guidelines. A strong positive correlation was observed between chest x-ray use and admission, while diagnostic uncertainty was moderately correlated with x-ray use. The audit emphasizes the importance of adhering to clinical guidelines to minimize unnecessary radiation exposure and highlights the need for further research and training to improve diagnostic confidence and clinical decision-making in this pediatric population.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:毛细支气管炎 是一种常见的下呼吸道感染,最常见的原因是 RSV,在一岁以下的婴儿中峰值为 发病率,男孩的发病率是女孩的 1.5-2 倍。它通常是自限性的,仅需要支持性治疗,但在某些情况下,可能会出现细菌感染、呼吸窘迫、缺氧和呼吸暂停等急性并发症,需要入院或进行医疗治疗。还可能出现后遗症,例如反复喘息和哮喘。经验不足或消息灵通的卫生专业人员可能会像成年人一样进行调查和管理,这可能导致儿童过度使用胸部 X 光检查以及本可避免的辐射暴露。英国国家临床卓越研究所 (NICE) 发布了 毛细支气管炎 管理指南,但缺乏遵守情况。“不要对患有 毛细支气管炎 的儿童进行常规胸部 X 光检查。” - 好的。方法:对 2026 年 1 月至 2026 年 4 月期间首次就诊且临床症状为 诊断 的临床 毛细支气管炎 到皇家阿尔伯特爱德华医院急症室儿科急诊科就诊的 0-24 个月婴儿进行回顾性临床审核。171 人中有 130 人符合标准。排除标准包括需要补充氧气、严重呼吸窘迫、患有慢性肺病、免疫缺陷、神经肌肉疾病、先天性心脏病等重大合并症以及两周内曾因相同疾病接受过 CXR 检查的患者。评估接受 CXR 的患者及其原因、谁进行了检查、是否入院以及临床不确定性。结果:130 名患者中有 16 名(12.3%)接受了胸部 X 光检查,130 名患者中有 12 名(9.2%)入院。根据 NICE 指南规定的标准,在接受胸部 X 光检查的人中,16 人中有 11 人(68.8%)没有正当理由。20% 的病例存在诊断不确定性。81.4%的病例第一评估级别为住院医生。在进行的胸部 X 光检查中,75% 的结果显示正常。81.8% 的不合理胸部 X 光检查报告为正常,同时 60% 的合理 CXR 报告为正常。在不合理的类别中注意到两个异常: 1. 双侧支气管周围壁轻度增厚。否则,无局灶性肺部病变。右心旁心旁小片状不明确的斑片状混浊可能提示早期感染过程。否则,肺部无局灶性病变。合理类别中注意到两个异常: 1. 右心后和右下区混浊轮廓增加 右半膈可能感染。轻微的支气管周围袖带提示小气道炎症。接受 CXR 的患者与入院患者之间存在很强的正相关性 φ = 0.528,p=0.0000031。接受 CXR 的患者与诊断不确定性 p=0.0006 之间存在统计显着的中等相关性。虽然第一位评估员通常是居民,但不存在统计相关性 (p=0.1915)。请参阅 CXR 表的原因(表 1)。结论:87.7% 的人没有接受胸部 X 光检查。这反映了大多数情况下合理的临床判断,但这低于 100% 的目标。一些潜在的原因可能是临床不确定性,在这种情况下 CXR 可以帮助区分。此次审计显示,信心级别更有可能是 CXR 请求的原因,而不是评估员级别。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 2 岁以下 毛细支气管炎 儿童不必要的胸部 X 光检查,特别检查胸部 X 光检查的使用频率、使用原因以及与入院和诊断不确定性的相关性。核心问题是胸部 X 光检查是否适合该儿科人群。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本次回顾性临床审计审查了2026年1月至2026年4月期间在皇家爱德华医院急诊科就诊的0-24个月婴儿,包括临床诊断为毛细支气管炎的患者,排除了需要补充氧气、严重呼吸窘迫、有显著合并症或过去2周内有胸部X光检查记录的患者。审计方法涉及评估胸部X光检查请求的原因、评估者级别、入院状态和诊断不确定性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审计发现,12.3%的患者接受了胸部X光检查,其中68.8%的患者没有按照NICE指南的正当理由接受了胸部X光检查。此外,75% 的胸部 X 光检查结果显示正常,并且胸部 X 光检查的使用与入院之间存在很强的正相关性 (φ = 0.528,p=0.0000031)。信心水平更有可能是要求进行胸部 X 光检查的原因,而不是评估者水平。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 胸部 X 光检查的使用与诊断不确定性之间存在统计学上显着的中度相关性 (p=0.0006)。然而,该综述并未提供有关具体诊断不确定性或这些不确定性对临床决策影响的详细信息。该研究也没有探讨不必要的胸部 X 光检查在辐射暴露或成本效益方面的潜在后果。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 此次审计强调需要更好地遵守 NICE 指南,以减少 毛细支气管炎 儿童不必要的胸部 X 光检查。它表明进一步的研究应侧重于了解诊断不确定性的原因并制定策略以改善此类病例的临床判断。此外,需要对卫生专业人员进行更好的教育和培训,以确保在这一人群中适当使用成像技术。

papers.title: Mucosal Vaccines Against Respiratory Viral Infections in Children: Current Advances, Challenges and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Respiratory viral infections remain a leading cause of morbidity, hospitalization, and healthcare burden among children worldwide. While traditional injectable vaccines have been effective in preventing severe disease, they are often limited in their ability to induce strong mucosal immunity at the initial sites of viral entry. Mucosal vaccination has therefore been proposed as a promising strategy to improve local and systemic immune responses and to potentially decrease pathogen transmission. The aim of this study is to review recent advances in mucosal vaccine development for pediatric populations, with an emphasis on the immunological basis of mucosal protection, features related to the age of the developing immune system, and the most relevant vaccine platforms, including intranasal, oral, viral-vectored, and nanoparticle-based approaches. We discuss recent advances in mucosal vaccine development against the main respiratory viral pathogens affecting children, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza viruses, and SARS-CoV-2, and review available preclinical and clinical evidence to support their use. Finally, we present major challenges limiting the widespread implementation of mucosal vaccines in pediatric populations, including safety, variability of immune responses, and regulatory considerations. We conclude by highlighting future directions and emerging technologies that may aid the development of safe, effective, and long-lasting mucosal vaccination strategies for the prevention of respiratory viral infections in children.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 我们讨论了粘膜 疫苗 针对影响儿童的主要呼吸道病毒病原体(包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)、流感病毒和 SARS-CoV-2)的最新进展,并回顾了现有的临床前和临床证据以支持其使用。

papers.title_zh: 粘膜 疫苗 对抗儿童呼吸道病毒感染:当前进展、挑战和未来前景
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory viral infections remain a leading cause of morbidity, hospitalization, and healthcare burden among children worldwide. While traditional injectable vaccines have been effective in preventing severe disease, they are often limited in their ability to induce strong mucosal immunity at the initial sites of viral entry. Mucosal vaccination has therefore been proposed as a promising strategy to improve local and systemic immune responses and to potentially decrease pathogen transmission. The aim of this study is to review recent advances in mucosal vaccine development for pediatric populations, with an emphasis on the immunological basis of mucosal protection, features related to the age of the developing immune system, and the most relevant vaccine platforms, including intranasal, oral, viral-vectored, and nanoparticle-based approaches. We discuss recent advances in mucosal vaccine development against the main respiratory viral pathogens affecting children, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza viruses, and SARS-CoV-2, and review available preclinical and clinical evidence to support their use. Finally, we present major challenges limiting the widespread implementation of mucosal vaccines in pediatric populations, including safety, variability of immune responses, and regulatory considerations. We conclude by highlighting future directions and emerging technologies that may aid the development of safe, effective, and long-lasting mucosal vaccination strategies for the prevention of respiratory viral infections in children.

papers.title: GUT MICROBIOTA PATTERNS IN PEDIATRIC RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF MICROBIAL SIGNATURES
papers.abstract: Early-life gut microbiota plays a crucial role in immune maturation and has been increasingly associated with host responses to infectious diseases. Emerging evidence highlights the gut–lung axis as an important component of pediatric respiratory health, yet child-focused syntheses remain limited. This systematic review with qualitative analysis summarizes recent original studies evaluating gut microbiota profiles in children with acute respiratory infections, providing a child-specific perspective distinct from reviews that combine age groups or focus on single pathogens. PubMed and the Virtual Health Library were systematically searched and the data were extracted using a structured matrix to identify patterns in microbial composition and methodological strengths and gaps. Twelve studies (2019–2025) including participants aged 0–18 years with conditions such as COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus infection, bronchiolitis, and recurrent respiratory tract infections met predefined inclusion criteria. Across studies, children with respiratory infections consistently exhibited gut dysbiosis, characterized by depletion of beneficial taxa and enrichment of pro-inflammatory genera. While methodological differences, including study design, sampling timing, and handling of confounders, limited direct quantitative comparisons, patterns of microbial alterations were identifiable. Overall, this review highlights a consistent association between gut microbiota alterations and pediatric respiratory infections, supporting the relevance of the gut–lung axis in early life. Nevertheless, methodological heterogeneity prevents inference about cause-and-effect relationships, highlighting the need for well-designed longitudinal and interventional studies to better understand the directionality of these associations.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the gut microbiota patterns in children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, specifically examining microbial signatures associated with RSV bronchiolitis and RSV infection. The central question is how gut microbiota alterations are linked to pediatric respiratory infections, particularly RSV-related conditions, and their role in immune responses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic search of PubMed and the Virtual Health Library, covering studies from 2019 to 2025. Data were extracted using a structured matrix to identify patterns in microbial composition and methodological strengths and gaps. The review included twelve studies with participants aged 0–18 years.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across the twelve studies, children with RSV infections consistently exhibited gut dysbiosis, characterized by depletion of beneficial taxa and enrichment of pro-inflammatory genera. This supports the relevance of the gut–lung axis in early life and highlights a consistent association between gut microbiota alterations and pediatric respiratory infections.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Methodological heterogeneity, including variations in study design, sampling timing, and handling of confounders, limited direct quantitative comparisons. This prevents inference about cause-and-effect relationships, indicating a need for more standardized and longitudinal studies to better understand the directionality of these associations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the importance of well-designed longitudinal and interventional studies to explore the causal relationships between gut microbiota and RSV infections. It also suggests the need for further research on microbial signatures in pediatric respiratory infections to inform targeted interventions and improve clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the gut microbiota patterns in children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, focusing on microbial signatures associated with RSV bronchiolitis and RSV infection. The review highlights a consistent association between gut dysbiosis and RSV-related respiratory conditions, emphasizing the role of the gut–lung axis in immune responses. However, methodological differences across studies limit direct quantitative comparisons and prevent causal inferences. The findings underscore the need for more standardized, longitudinal, and interventional research to better understand the relationship between gut microbiota and RSV infections, with potential implications for targeted interventions and improved clinical outcomes in pediatric populations.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对 PubMed 和虚拟健康图书馆进行了系统检索,涵盖 2019 年至 2025 年的研究。使用结构化矩阵提取数据,以确定微生物组成模式以及方法学优势和差距。该综述包括 12 项研究,参与者年龄为 0-18 岁。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染儿童的肠道微生物群模式,特别检查与 RSV 毛细支气管炎 和 RSV 感染相关的微生物特征。核心问题是肠道微生物群的改变如何与儿童呼吸道感染(特别是 RSV 相关疾病)相关,以及它们在 免疫应答 中的作用。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对 PubMed 和虚拟健康图书馆进行了系统检索,涵盖 2019 年至 2025 年的研究。使用结构化矩阵提取数据,以确定微生物组成模式以及方法学优势和差距。该综述包括 12 项研究,参与者年龄为 0-18 岁。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在这 12 项研究中,RSV 感染的儿童始终表现出肠道菌群失调,其特征是有益类群的消耗和促炎菌属的富集。这支持了生命早期肠肺轴的相关性,并强调了肠道微生物群改变与儿童呼吸道感染之间的一致关联。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 方法学异质性,包括研究设计、采样时间和混杂因素处理的差异,限制了直接定量比较。这阻碍了对因果关系的推断,表明需要进行更标准化和纵向的研究,以更好地理解这些关联的方向性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调了精心设计的纵向和介入研究的重要性,以探索肠道微生物群与 RSV 感染之间的因果关系。它还表明需要对儿科呼吸道感染的微生物特征进行进一步研究,以便为有针对性的干预措施提供信息并改善临床结果。

papers.title: MATERNAL RSV VACCINATION AND CLINICAL SEVERITY OF RSV-POSITIVE BRONCHIOLITIS IN CHILDREN ADMITTED TO THE PAEDIATRIC WARD: A RETROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY
papers.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of bronchiolitis requiring hospital admission in infants. Maternal RSV vaccination was introduced in the UK in September 2024 to reduce severe RSV disease during early infancy. This retrospective study evaluated the clinical characteristics of children admitted with RSV-positive bronchiolitis in relation to maternal RSV immunisation status and the association between maternal RSV vaccination and respiratory support and length of hospital stay. Methods Children admitted with laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive bronchiolitis between October 2025 and February 2026 across two hospitals within the Trust were included in the study. Maternal RSV vaccination status was obtained from BadgerNet electronic records. Children’s data were collected from electronic patient records. Data collected included age at presentation, respiratory support, and duration of hospital stay. Respiratory support was categorised as no respiratory support, low-flow oxygen (LFO2), or high-flow nasal oxygen (AIRVO). Results A total of 97 children were admitted with RSV-positive bronchiolitis. Maternal RSV vaccination status was available for 90 children; 37 (41%) were born to vaccinated mothers and 53 (59%) to unvaccinated mothers. In the vaccinated group, 24 (64.9%) children were aged 0–6 months, 12 (32.4%) were aged 6–12 months, and only one (2.7%) was older than 12 months. In contrast, among children born to unvaccinated mothers, 19 (36%) were aged 0–6 months, 8 (15%) were aged 6–12 months, and 26 (49%) were older than 12 months. However, the number of infants younger than 2 months with RSV infection was lower in the vaccinated group than in the unvaccinated group (4 vs 11 children). Thus, among infants and children whose mothers had received the RSV vaccine, almost all admissions (97.3%) occurred before 12 months of age. In contrast, almost half of admissions (49%) in the unvaccinated group occurred in children older than 12 months. Children whose mothers had received the RSV vaccine appeared to require less respiratory support overall. The proportion requiring no respiratory support was higher in the vaccinated group than in the unvaccinated group (62.2% vs 49%). Low-flow oxygen was required in 27.0% of children in the vaccinated group compared with 36% in the unvaccinated group. Similarly, AIRVO (high-flow nasal oxygen) was required in 10.8% of children in the vaccinated group compared with 15% in the unvaccinated group. There was a statistically significant association between vaccination status and length of hospital stay (χ2 = 12.83, p = 0.0016). Children whose mother had received the vaccine were more likely to have a hospital stay of 3 days (50.9% vs 18.9%). Limitations This was an observational analysis, and potential confounding factors were not included, including prematurity, underlying comorbidities and the timing of maternal RSV vaccination. The difference in age distribution between the two groups may have influenced the results. Conclusions Children born to mothers who received the RSV vaccine appeared to require less respiratory support and had statistically significant shorter hospital stays. Fewer children in the vaccinated group appeared to require escalation to AIRVO, suggesting a potential reduction in the severity of bronchiolitis. These findings suggest an association between maternal RSV vaccination and reduced disease severity and healthcare utilisation.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study investigated the clinical characteristics of children admitted with RSV-positive bronchiolitis in relation to maternal RSV immunisation status. The study was conducted across two hospitals in the UK between October 2025 and February 2026, involving 97 children. Maternal vaccination status was available for 90 children, with 41% born to vaccinated mothers and 59% to unvaccinated mothers. The study found that vaccinated mothers were more likely to have children admitted before 12 months of age, and that children of vaccinated mothers required less respiratory support and had shorter hospital stays. However, the study had limitations, including its observational design and lack of control for confounding factors such as prematurity and comorbidities. The findings suggest a potential association between maternal RSV vaccination and reduced disease severity, which could inform future strategies for RSV prevention in infants.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿 毛细支气管炎 需要入院的主要原因。本研究旨在评估 RSV 阳性 毛细支气管炎 入院儿童的临床特征与母亲 RSV 免疫状态的关系,以及母亲 RSV 毛细支气管炎 与呼吸支持和住院时间之间的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性观察研究是在 2025 年 10 月至 2026 年 2 月期间在信托基金内的两家医院进行的。共有 97 名患有 RSV 阳性 毛细支气管炎 的儿童入院,其中 90 名儿童的母亲 RSV 毛细支气管炎 状态可用。
elements_zh.methods: 儿童数据从电子病历中收集,母亲 RSV 疫苗接种 状态从 BadgerNet 电子记录中获取。收集的数据包括就诊时的年龄、呼吸支持和住院时间。
elements_zh.main_results: 90 名儿童的母亲 RSV 疫苗接种 状态可用;37 例 (41%) 是接种疫苗的母亲所生,53 例 (59%) 是未接种疫苗的母亲所生。接种组中感染 RSV 的 2 个月以下婴儿数量低于未接种组(4 例 vs 11 例)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明母体 RSV 疫苗接种 与疾病严重程度和医疗保健利用率降低之间存在关联。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能为婴儿 RSV 预防和管理的未来策略提供参考,特别是关于母亲 疫苗接种 在减少呼吸支持需求和缩短住院时间方面的潜在益处。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这是一项观察性分析,不包括潜在的混杂因素,包括早产、潜在的合并症和母体 RSV 疫苗接种 的时间。由于观察性质和缺乏对混杂变量的控制,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Clinical and Laboratory Characteristics of RSV-Positive and RSV-Negative Bronchiolitis in Hospitalized Children Younger Than Two Years: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Objective: To compare the demographic, clinical and laboratory characteristics of hospitalized children with RSV-positive and RSV-negative bronchiolitis. Methodology: This comparative cross-sectional study included 60 children younger than two years admitted with bronchiolitis to a tertiary-care hospital in Islamabad from November 2025 to April 2026. RSV status was determined by viral polymerase chain reaction (PCR), with 30 children in each group. Clinical severity was assessed using the Wood-Downes-Ferrés (WDF) score. Two-sided comparisons were recalculated from available group summaries. Results: Children with RSV-positive bronchiolitis were younger than RSV-negative children (3.9 ± 3.2 vs 8.9 ± 9.8 months; p=0.012). Cough and fever were common in both groups. More than two presenting symptoms were reported more often in the RSV-negative group (73.3% vs 43.3%; p=0.035). Mean WDF score was higher in the RSV-positive group (5.9 ± 2.2 vs 4.4 ± 2.4; p=0.014). Total leukocyte count was numerically higher (12.2 ± 3.7 vs 10.5 ± 3.1 ×109/L), although this difference was not statistically significant on recalculation (p=0.059). C-reactive protein positivity was identical in both groups (50.0%). Conclusions: Hospitalized children with RSV-positive bronchiolitis were younger and had higher unadjusted bedside respiratory severity scores. Presenting symptoms and routine blood findings overlapped substantially. No quantitative PCR viral-load information was available, and no age- or sex-stratified assessment could be reconstructed. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because age-adjusted analyses and individual severity categories were unavailable. The study describes differences between hospitalized groups rather than proving that RSV independently determines severity at the time of admission in this single-center comparison.
papers.journal: Annals of PIMS-Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University

papers.title: Respiratory Pathogen Positivity in Children: Shifting Patterns at a Single Children’s Hospital in Hangzhou, China, 2024–2025
papers.abstract: Respiratory infections are frequently encountered in children and constitute an important threat to pediatric health. Monitoring temporal shifts in the circulating pathogen spectrum is consequently important for informing effective prevention and treatment strategies. To assess changes in respiratory pathogen test positivity among tested children during 2024–2025, we examined respiratory pathogen testing data obtained from patients attending a large children’s hospital in eastern China, with results stratified according to pathogen, age group, and month of onset. Human rhinovirus (HRV) remained the most commonly detected pathogen in both 2024 (10,268/47,650; 21.55%) and 2025 (10,634/50,627; 21.00%). In 2024, Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) ranked second (9663/47,650; 20.28%), whereas its detection rate decreased substantially in 2025 (1647/50,627; 3.25%). In contrast, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; 8058/50,627; 15.92%) and influenza A virus (InfA; 4424/50,627; 8.74%) became more prominent in 2025, occupying the second and third positions, respectively, after HRV. Children aged 1–3 years represented a consistently large proportion of respiratory infections. Beyond 3 years of age, however, the pathogen profile shifted, with the most evident change being an age-related rise in InfA infections. The number of cases recorded during winter also increased substantially in 2025 relative to 2024. The potential roles of climate variability, vaccination coverage, and other factors in these epidemiological changes require further investigation. These single-center test-positive findings should not be interpreted as regional positivity rate among tested children. Prevention and control measures for pediatric respiratory infections should therefore account for changes in the pathogen spectrum, particularly among high-risk age groups and during seasonal peaks.

Human rhinovirus (HRV) remained the most common pathogen, while Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) decreased significantly in 2025. papers.title: Post-pandemic shifts in respiratory pathogens and peripheral immune correlates among hospitalized children with ALRTI: a retrospective molecular surveillance study in northern China, 2023–2024
papers.abstract: Background Post-pandemic respiratory pathogen circulation has changed, but concurrent molecular and immune data remain limited. We examined pathogen trends and peripheral immune correlates in children hospitalized with acute lower respiratory tract infection (ALRTI) in northern China during 2023–2024. Methods This single-centre retrospective study included 604 hospitalization episodes. A 13-target multiplex nucleic-acid panel defined pathogen groups. Immunoglobulins, lymphocyte subsets and inflammatory markers were compared across monoinfection, mixed infection (≥2 pathogen categories) and panel-negative groups. Immune comparisons adjusted for age, sex and year using regression with cluster-robust standard errors for repeated admissions and false-discovery-rate correction. Annual trends were assessed using age-standardised rates and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and calendar month. Results Among 601 complete-panel episodes, 528 (87.9%) had a detected pathogen. Mycoplasma pneumoniae predominated (43.4%), followed by rhinovirus (23.6%) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; 14.3%). pneumoniae detection increased from 32.4% in 2023 to 54.3% in 2024, while RSV decreased from 21.4% to 7.3% (both q < 0.001). Annual shifts persisted after age standardisation and covariate adjustment: adjusted odds ratios for 2024 vs. 2023 were 3.09 (95% CI, 1.94–4.94) for M. pneumoniae, 0.29 (0.16–0.53) for RSV and 0.13 (0.03–0.53) for influenza A. Mixed infection (21.5%) decreased with age (adjusted odds ratio per year, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.86–0.98). After adjustment and multiplicity correction, M. pneumoniae and mixed infections were associated with higher immunoglobulin M. Rhinovirus monoinfection was associated with lower total T-cell and CD8+ T-cell percentages and higher B-cell percentage; mixed infection was associated with lower total T-cell percentage. Cytokine analyses were exploratory because approximately 35% of episodes were tested. Conclusion Pathogen profiles shifted substantially between 2023 and 2024, supporting continued molecular surveillance and age-aware interpretation of immune measures. Because the panel did not cover typical bacterial pathogens, panel-negative episodes should not be equated with absence of infection.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Pathogen profiles shifted substantially between 2023 and 2024, supporting continued molecular surveillance and age-aware interpretation of immune measures.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously inform the need for ongoing molecular surveillance and age-specific interpretation of immune correlates in respiratory infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-centre design and potential biases from repeated admissions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on retrospective data and the use of adjusted odds ratios.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates post-pandemic shifts in respiratory pathogens and immune correlates among hospitalized children with acute lower respiratory tract infection (ALRTI) in northern China during 2023–2024. A 13-target multiplex nucleic-acid panel identified pathogen groups, revealing that Mycoplasma pneumoniae increased in prevalence while respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) decreased. The study highlights the importance of molecular surveillance and age-aware interpretation of immune measures. However, the single-centre design and potential biases from repeated admissions limit the confidence in the findings, resulting in a moderate evidence strength assessment.

papers.title_zh: 大流行后 ALRTI 住院儿童呼吸道病原体和外周免疫相关性的变化:2023-2024 年中国北方地区回顾性分子 监测 研究
papers.source_body_en: Background Post-pandemic respiratory pathogen circulation has changed, but concurrent molecular and immune data remain limited. We examined pathogen trends and peripheral immune correlates in children hospitalized with acute lower respiratory tract infection (ALRTI) in northern China during 2023–2024. Methods This single-centre retrospective study included 604 hospitalization episodes. A 13-target multiplex nucleic-acid panel defined pathogen groups. Immunoglobulins, lymphocyte subsets and inflammatory markers were compared across monoinfection, mixed infection (≥2 pathogen categories) and panel-negative groups. Immune comparisons adjusted for age, sex and year using regression with cluster-robust standard errors for repeated admissions and false-discovery-rate correction. Annual trends were assessed using age-standardised rates and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and calendar month. Results Among 601 complete-panel episodes, 528 (87.9%) had a detected pathogen. Mycoplasma pneumoniae predominated (43.4%), followed by rhinovirus (23.6%) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; 14.3%). pneumoniae detection increased from 32.4% in 2023 to 54.3% in 2024, while RSV decreased from 21.4% to 7.3% (both q < 0.001). Annual shifts persisted after age standardisation and covariate adjustment: adjusted odds ratios for 2024 vs. 2023 were 3.09 (95% CI, 1.94–4.94) for M. pneumoniae, 0.29 (0.16–0.53) for RSV and 0.13 (0.03–0.53) for influenza A. Mixed infection (21.5%) decreased with age (adjusted odds ratio per year, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.86–0.98). After adjustment and multiplicity correction, M. pneumoniae and mixed infections were associated with higher immunoglobulin M. Rhinovirus monoinfection was associated with lower total T-cell and CD8+ T-cell percentages and higher B-cell percentage; mixed infection was associated with lower total T-cell percentage. Cytokine analyses were exploratory because approximately 35% of episodes were tested. Conclusion Pathogen profiles shifted substantially between 2023 and 2024, supporting continued molecular surveillance and age-aware interpretation of immune measures. Because the panel did not cover typical bacterial pathogens, panel-negative episodes should not be equated with absence of infection.

papers.title: Impact of Nasopharyngeal Swab Freezing Storage on the Detection of Common Respiratory Viral Molecular Targets
papers.abstract: Archived respiratory specimens are valuable biological samples for retrospective diagnostic studies and assay validation. However, long-term storage may affect viral nucleic acid integrity and molecular detection, which is an issue of particular relevance for RNA viruses, whose RNA genomes may be particularly susceptible to storage-related degradation. The present study evaluates the quality and stability of nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) aliquots stored at −80 °C for at least one year in our biobank and subsequently retested for the same viral RNA targets. NPS previously tested for SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus, or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were retested using a fully automated sample-to-result molecular platform integrating nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and viral target detection in different multiplex assay formats. As the stored samples were tested using an assay different from the one used for the corresponding fresh samples, discordant results were further assessed using a third independent molecular assay. Qualitative results were compared with previous testing to assess diagnostic agreement, and changes in cycle threshold (Ct) values were analyzed. Target SARS-CoV-2 showed the highest stability, with positive percent agreement (PPA) of 97.1–98.6% and Ct increases of 2.08–3.03 cycles across assay formats. RSV showed intermediate stability, with a PPA of 88.4–97.1% and Ct increases of 1.75–5.20 cycles. Influenza showed the greatest signal loss, with PPA of 80.0–92.9% and mean Ct increases of 5.47–7.92 cycles. The Ct increases after storage were significant for all viral targets. Differences between assay configurations indicated that assay formulation and target characteristics may influence post-storage performance. Respiratory swab aliquots stored at −80° C can support retrospective molecular testing, although storage-related signal loss varies according to the viral target and assay configuration. These effects should be considered when interpreting results from archived specimens.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved retesting nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) aliquots stored at −80 °C for at least one year in a biobank, focusing on RSV and other common respiratory viruses.
analysis.methods: Stored NPS samples were retested using a fully automated sample-to-result molecular platform, and discordant results were further assessed with a third independent molecular assay to ensure accuracy.
analysis.main_results: RSV showed intermediate stability with a positive percent agreement (PPA) of 88.4–97.1% and Ct increases of 1.75–5.20 cycles. Influenza showed the greatest signal loss with a PPA of 80.0–92.9% and mean Ct increases of 5.47–7.92 cycles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that storage-related signal loss varies depending on the viral target and assay configuration, emphasizing the need for careful interpretation of archived specimens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the cautious use of archived respiratory specimens for molecular testing, particularly for RSV, and suggest the importance of considering assay-specific factors in diagnostic accuracy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to archived specimens and does not account for real-time viral load or environmental factors, but the evidence is moderate due to the controlled setting and multiple assay validations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of long-term freezing storage on the detection of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other common respiratory viruses. It evaluates the stability of nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) aliquots stored at −80 °C for at least one year and retested using a fully automated molecular platform. Results show that RSV exhibits intermediate stability with a positive percent agreement (PPA) of 88.4–97.1% and cycle threshold (Ct) increases of 1.75–5.20 cycles, while influenza shows the greatest signal loss with a PPA of 80.0–92.9% and mean Ct increases of 5.47–7.92 cycles. The study underscores the variability in post-storage performance based on viral targets and assay configurations, suggesting that archived specimens should be interpreted with caution. The findings are of moderate evidence strength due to the controlled setting and multiple assay validations, but the study does not account for real-time viral load or environmental factors.

papers.source_body_en: Archived respiratory specimens are valuable biological samples for retrospective diagnostic studies and assay validation. However, long-term storage may affect viral nucleic acid integrity and molecular detection, which is an issue of particular relevance for RNA viruses, whose RNA genomes may be particularly susceptible to storage-related degradation. The present study evaluates the quality and stability of nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) aliquots stored at −80 °C for at least one year in our biobank and subsequently retested for the same viral RNA targets. NPS previously tested for SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus, or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were retested using a fully automated sample-to-result molecular platform integrating nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and viral target detection in different multiplex assay formats. As the stored samples were tested using an assay different from the one used for the corresponding fresh samples, discordant results were further assessed using a third independent molecular assay. Qualitative results were compared with previous testing to assess diagnostic agreement, and changes in cycle threshold (Ct) values were analyzed. Target SARS-CoV-2 showed the highest stability, with positive percent agreement (PPA) of 97.1–98.6% and Ct increases of 2.08–3.03 cycles across assay formats. RSV showed intermediate stability, with a PPA of 88.4–97.1% and Ct increases of 1.75–5.20 cycles. Influenza showed the greatest signal loss, with PPA of 80.0–92.9% and mean Ct increases of 5.47–7.92 cycles. The Ct increases after storage were significant for all viral targets. Differences between assay configurations indicated that assay formulation and target characteristics may influence post-storage performance. Respiratory swab aliquots stored at −80° C can support retrospective molecular testing, although storage-related signal loss varies according to the viral target and assay configuration. These effects should be considered when interpreting results from archived specimens.
papers.abstract_zh: 存档的呼吸道标本是用于回顾性诊断研究和测定验证的宝贵生物样本。然而,长期储存可能会影响病毒核酸完整性和分子检测,这对于 RNA 病毒来说尤其重要,其 RNA 基因组 可能特别容易受到储存相关降解的影响。本研究评估了鼻咽拭子 (NPS) 等分试样的质量和稳定性,该等分试样在我们的生物库中于 -80 °C 下保存至少一年,随后重新测试相同的病毒 RNA 靶标。使用全自动样本到结果分子平台重新测试之前针对 SARS-CoV-2、流感病毒或 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 进行的 NPS,该平台以不同的多重检测格式集成了核酸提取、扩增和病毒靶点检测。由于使用与相应新鲜样品所用的检测方法不同的检测方法对储存的样品进行测试,因此使用第三种独立的分子检测方法进一步评估了不一致的结果。将定性结果与之前的测试进行比较以评估诊断一致性,并分析循环阈值 (Ct) 值的变化。目标 SARS-CoV-2 显示出最高的稳定性,各种检测格式的阳性一致性百分比 (PPA) 为 97.1-98.6%,Ct 增加 2.08-3.03 个循环。RSV 显示出中等稳定性,PPA 为 88.4-97.1%,Ct 增加了 1.75-5.20 个循环。流感显示出最大的信号损失,PPA 为 80.0-92.9%,平均 Ct 增加 5.47-7.92 个周期。对于所有病毒靶点来说,储存后的 Ct 增加都很显着。测定配置之间的差异表明测定配方和目标特性可能会影响存储后的性能。尽管与存储相关的信号损失根据病毒靶点和检测配置而变化,但储存在-80°C下的呼吸道拭子等分试样可以支持回顾性分子检测。在解释存档样本的结果时应考虑这些影响。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估长期冷冻储存对病毒分子靶点检测的影响,特别是呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV),因为储存可能会影响核酸完整性和分子检测。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及重新测试在生物库中在 -80°C 下保存至少一年的鼻咽拭子 (NPS) 等分试样,重点关注 RSV 和其他常见呼吸道病毒。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用全自动样本到结果分子平台对存储的 NPS 样本进行重新测试,并使用第三个独立分子测定进一步评估不一致的结果,以确保准确性。
analysis_zh.main_results: RSV 显示出中等稳定性,正一致性百分比 (PPA) 为 88.4-97.1%,Ct 增加为 1.75-5.20 个循环。流感显示出最大的信号损失,PPA 为 80.0-92.9%,平均 Ct 增加为 5.47-7.92 个周期。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,与存储相关的信号丢失因病毒靶标和检测配置而异,强调需要仔细解释存档的样本。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,应谨慎使用存档的呼吸道标本进行分子检测,尤其是 RSV 检测,并表明在诊断准确性中考虑特定检测因素的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于存档的标本,没有考虑实时病毒载量或环境因素,但由于受控设置和多重测定验证,证据是温和的。

papers.title: Impacto de la vacunación materna en lactantes con bronquiolitis ingresados con soporte respiratorio. Centro Hospitalario Pereira Rossell. Uruguay. Invierno, 2025
papers.abstract: To analyze the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) perfusion protein F in infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center during the winter of 2025. An analytical, observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study was conducted, including infants under 12 months of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support, divided into two groups according to maternal vaccination status. Clinical characteristics associated with worse disease progression and severity were analyzed. Quantitative variables were presented as medians and interquartile ranges or means and standard deviations, and qualitative variables as absolute and relative frequencies. Mann-Whitney U test, t-test, Fisher’s exact test, and chi-square test were applied, depending on the type of variable, to compare both groups (patients whose mothers were vaccinated vs. those whose mothers were not). A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Two hundred and twenty-six patients were included, mostly male (136, 60%), and 176 (79%) had RSV. The proportion of vaccinated mothers was 44 (19%). The median age was lower in patients whose mothers were vaccinated (3 months, range 2–5) vs. 5 months (range 3–9), p < 0.001. No significant differences were observed between the groups for clinical variables at admission or those associated with a worse outcome. Conclusions: The lower proportion of infants with unvaccinated mothers may suggest a greater impact of this vaccine on the risk of hospitalization. Further studies including other variables are needed for a better understanding of this strategy.
papers.journal: Anales de la Facultad de Medicina

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) on infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support. This is relevant due to the high burden of RSV-related hospitalizations in young infants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study was conducted at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center in Uruguay during the winter of 2025, including infants under 12 months of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support, stratified by maternal vaccination status.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed clinical characteristics associated with disease progression and severity, using quantitative variables presented as medians and interquartile ranges or means and standard deviations, and qualitative variables as absolute and relative frequencies. Statistical tests including Mann-Whitney U test, t-test, Fisher’s exact test, and chi-square test were applied to compare the groups.
analysis.main_results: The median age was significantly lower in infants whose mothers were vaccinated (3 months, range 2–5) compared to those whose mothers were not (5 months, range 3–9), p < 0.001. No significant differences were observed between the groups for clinical variables at admission or those associated with a worse outcome.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that the lower proportion of infants with unvaccinated mothers may indicate a potential protective effect of maternal vaccination against RSV. However, they emphasize the need for further studies to better understand this strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform public health strategies regarding maternal vaccination to reduce the risk of RSV-related hospitalizations in infants. They highlight the importance of considering maternal vaccination status in the management of RSV bronchiolitis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and does not establish causality. The evidence is limited by the lack of control for confounding variables, and the results should be interpreted with caution due to the potential for bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) on infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center in Uruguay during the winter of 2025. It was an observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study comparing infants based on their mothers' vaccination status. The median age was significantly lower in vaccinated mothers' infants (3 months) compared to non-vaccinated mothers' infants (5 months), but no significant differences were observed in clinical variables at admission or outcomes. The authors suggest that maternal vaccination may reduce the risk of hospitalization, though they acknowledge the need for further studies to confirm this. The study's limitations include its observational nature and lack of control for confounding factors, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估母亲 疫苗接种 与 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 对需要呼吸支持的 1 岁以下婴儿的影响。这是因为小婴儿因 RSV 相关住院的负担很高。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年冬季,乌拉圭佩雷拉·罗塞尔医院中心进行了一项观察性、纵向、双重性 队列研究 研究,研究对象包括 12 个月以下、需要呼吸支持的 毛细支气管炎 婴儿,并按母亲 疫苗接种 状态进行分层。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用以中位数和四分位数范围或平均值和标准差表示的定量变量,以及以绝对和相对频率表示的定性变量,分析了与疾病进展和严重程度相关的临床特征。采用Mann-Whitney U检验、t检验、Fisher精确检验和卡方检验等统计检验来比较各组。
elements_zh.main_results: 与母亲未接种疫苗的婴儿(5 个月,范围 3-9)相比,母亲接种疫苗的婴儿(3 个月,范围 2-5)的婴儿中位年龄显着较低,p < 0.001。入院时的临床变量或与较差结果相关的临床变量在各组之间没有观察到显着差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,母亲未接种疫苗的婴儿比例较低可能表明母亲 疫苗接种 对 RSV 具有潜在的保护作用。然而,他们强调需要进一步研究以更好地理解这一策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能为有关孕产妇 疫苗接种 的公共卫生策略提供信息,以降低婴儿因 RSV 相关住院的风险。他们强调了在 RSV 毛细支气管炎 管理中考虑母亲 疫苗接种 状态的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,并未建立因果关系。由于缺乏对混杂变量的控制,证据受到限制,由于可能存在偏差,结果应谨慎解释。

papers.title_zh: 影响母亲的真空和乳汁对支气管炎的影响,并影响呼吸系统。佩雷拉·罗塞尔中心医院。乌拉圭。因维耶诺,2025
papers.source_body_en: To analyze the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) perfusion protein F in infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center during the winter of 2025. An analytical, observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study was conducted, including infants under 12 months of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support, divided into two groups according to maternal vaccination status. Clinical characteristics associated with worse disease progression and severity were analyzed. Quantitative variables were presented as medians and interquartile ranges or means and standard deviations, and qualitative variables as absolute and relative frequencies. Mann-Whitney U test, t-test, Fisher’s exact test, and chi-square test were applied, depending on the type of variable, to compare both groups (patients whose mothers were vaccinated vs. those whose mothers were not). A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Two hundred and twenty-six patients were included, mostly male (136, 60%), and 176 (79%) had RSV. The proportion of vaccinated mothers was 44 (19%). The median age was lower in patients whose mothers were vaccinated (3 months, range 2–5) vs. 5 months (range 3–9), p < 0.001. Conclusions: The lower proportion of infants with unvaccinated mothers may suggest a greater impact of this vaccine on the risk of hospitalization. analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用以中位数和四分位数范围或平均值和标准差表示的定量变量,以及以绝对和相对频率表示的定性变量,分析了与疾病进展和严重程度相关的临床特征。采用Mann-Whitney U检验、t检验、Fisher精确检验和卡方检验等统计检验来比较各组。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与母亲未接种疫苗的婴儿(5 个月,范围 3-9)相比,母亲接种疫苗的婴儿(3 个月,范围 2-5)的婴儿中位年龄显着较低,p < 0.001。入院时的临床变量或与较差结果相关的临床变量在各组之间没有观察到显着差异。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,并未建立因果关系。由于缺乏对混杂变量的控制,证据受到限制,由于可能存在偏差,结果应谨慎解释。

papers.title: PREDICTORS OF NON-INVASIVE VENTILATION (NIV) FAILURE IN INFANTS AND CHILDREN WITH BRONCHIOLITIS
papers.abstract: Background: Bronchiolitis is a major cause of hospitalization and critical care admission in infants and young children. Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is increasingly used for respiratory support, but predictors of NIV failure in bronchiolitis remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify predictors of NIV failure in children younger than 2 years hospitalized with bronchiolitis. Methods: A bidirectional study was conducted at the Royal Hospital, Oman, over three bronchiolitis seasons from October 2023 to February 2026. Children younger than 2 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit or high-dependency unit with bronchiolitis requiring NIV were included. Demographic, clinical, radiological, virological, and physiological variables were collected. NIV failure was defined as the need for endotracheal intubation. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of NIV failure. Results: Of 330 children, 46 (13.9%) required intubation, while 284 (86.1%) were successfully managed with NIV. Independent predictors of NIV failure were RSV infection (aOR 2.75, 95% CI 1.25–6.06; P=0.012), radiographic lobar collapse (aOR 3.81, 95% CI 1.70–8.52; P=0.001), apnea (aOR 4.71, 95% CI 1.39–15.99; P=0.013), and higher pCO2 one hour after NIV initiation (aOR 1.05 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.01–1.10; P=0.010). Median time to intubation was 15 hours. Patients who failed NIV had a longer median critical care stay than those who succeeded (9.5 vs 5 days; P<0.001). Conclusion: NIV was successful in most children with bronchiolitis. RSV infection, lobar collapse, apnea, and higher pCO2 one hour after NIV initiation were independently associated with NIV failure. Early recognition of these predictors may help identify children requiring closer monitoring and timely escalation of respiratory support.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify predictors of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) failure in children younger than 2 years hospitalized with bronchiolitis. Conducted at the Royal Hospital, Oman, over three bronchiolitis seasons from October 2023 to February 2026, the study included children admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit or high-dependency unit requiring NIV. Demographic, clinical, radiological, virological, and physiological variables were collected, and NIV failure was defined as the need for endotracheal intubation. Logistic regression analyses identified RSV infection, radiographic lobar collapse, apnea, and higher pCO2 one hour after NIV initiation as independent predictors of NIV failure. The study found that 13.9% of children required intubation, while 86.1% were successfully managed with NIV. The median time to intubation was 15 hours, and patients who failed NIV had a longer median critical care stay than those who succeeded. The findings suggest that early recognition of these predictors may help identify children requiring closer monitoring and timely escalation of respiratory support. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of reported limitations.

papers.title_zh: 毛细支气管炎 婴儿和儿童无创通气 (NIV) 失败的预测因素
papers.source_body_en: Background: Bronchiolitis is a major cause of hospitalization and critical care admission in infants and young children. Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is increasingly used for respiratory support, but predictors of NIV failure in bronchiolitis remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify predictors of NIV failure in children younger than 2 years hospitalized with bronchiolitis. Methods: A bidirectional study was conducted at the Royal Hospital, Oman, over three bronchiolitis seasons from October 2023 to February 2026. Children younger than 2 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit or high-dependency unit with bronchiolitis requiring NIV were included. Demographic, clinical, radiological, virological, and physiological variables were collected. NIV failure was defined as the need for endotracheal intubation. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of NIV failure. Results: Of 330 children, 46 (13.9%) required intubation, while 284 (86.1%) were successfully managed with NIV. Independent predictors of NIV failure were RSV infection (aOR 2.75, 95% CI 1.25–6.06; P=0.012), radiographic lobar collapse (aOR 3.81, 95% CI 1.70–8.52; P=0.001), apnea (aOR 4.71, 95% CI 1.39–15.99; P=0.013), and higher pCO2 one hour after NIV initiation (aOR 1.05 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.01–1.10; P=0.010). Median time to intubation was 15 hours. Patients who failed NIV had a longer median critical care stay than those who succeeded (9.5 vs 5 days; P<0.001). Conclusion: NIV was successful in most children with bronchiolitis. RSV infection, lobar collapse, apnea, and higher pCO2 one hour after NIV initiation were independently associated with NIV failure. Early recognition of these predictors may help identify children requiring closer monitoring and timely escalation of respiratory support.

papers.title: Immune checkpoint modulation beyond cancer: a conceptual framework for small-molecule host-directed antiviral therapy
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoints are important regulators of antiviral immunity, but their roles in viral infections are more complex than the conventional model of immune inhibition. Although sustained checkpoint signaling can impair antiviral T-cell function and contribute to viral persistence, it can also limit immune-mediated tissue damage. This dual role presents a major challenge for therapeutic intervention, as indiscriminate checkpoint inhibition may improve viral control at the expense of increased immunopathology. In this review, we examine how viral infections reshape immune checkpoint networks through antiviral signaling, protein homeostasis, cellular metabolism, and tissue-specific immune regulation. We discuss the implications of these mechanisms for chronic viral infections, including human immunodeficiency virus and hepatitis B and C viruses, as well as acute respiratory infections caused by influenza A virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, and respiratory syncytial virus. Particular attention is given to small-molecule checkpoint modulators and their potential to regulate protein interactions, stability, localization, and signaling beyond conventional receptor–ligand blockade. We distinguish the pharmacological evidence supporting these compounds, which is derived primarily from oncology-related research, from the much more limited evidence of their direct antiviral activity. However, direct evidence that these compounds can achieve effective checkpoint modulation while improving viral control and limiting tissue injury remains limited. We therefore discuss the need for rigorous target validation and a more precise approach to patient selection and treatment design. Integrating viral burden, antiviral T-cell function, checkpoint activity, and inflammatory status may help identify patients most likely to benefit from intervention and guide treatment timing, intensity, and discontinuation. Combining checkpoint modulation with direct-acting antivirals or other host-directed therapies may offer additional benefits if viral suppression and immune restoration can be appropriately balanced. A shift from sustained checkpoint blockade toward context-dependent immune modulation may provide a basis for developing more precise host-directed antiviral strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the complex role of immune checkpoints in antiviral immunity, particularly in the context of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections. It highlights the dual nature of checkpoint signaling, which can both impair antiviral T-cell function and limit immune-mediated tissue damage. The review emphasizes the need for a nuanced understanding of these mechanisms to develop effective therapeutic strategies. While small-molecule checkpoint modulators show potential in regulating immune responses, their direct antiviral activity remains limited, necessitating further research. The article calls for rigorous target validation and a more precise approach to patient selection and treatment design, suggesting that integrating viral burden, T-cell function, checkpoint activity, and inflammatory status could guide interventions. The review also discusses the possibility of combining checkpoint modulation with direct-acting antivirals or other host-directed therapies to achieve a balance between viral suppression and immune restoration.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Upper Respiratory Tract Infections and the Incidence of Acute Otitis Media in Children: A Literature Review
papers.abstract: Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) is one of the most common illnesses in children and may lead to complications, one of which is acute otitis media (AOM). Children are more susceptible to AOM because their Eustachian tubes are relatively shorter and more horizontal, with immature drainage function. URTI can cause inflammation and edema of the nasopharynx, impairing Eustachian tube function and increasing the risk of AOM. This study was a literature review. A total of 10 journals published between 2021 and 2025 were reviewed and synthesized to determine the association between URTI and AOM in children, including relevant risk factors and pathogens. The review showed an association between URTI and AOM in children. (2025) reported a statistically significant association with a p-value of 0.019, while Azzahra et al. (2025) reported a p-value of 0.033 with a PR of 1.35. Several viruses, particularly respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus, were associated with AOM. Age, Eustachian tube anatomy, exposure to cigarette smoke, and air pollution may also increase the risk of AOM.URTI is associated with the occurrence of AOM in children through an inflammatory process that impairs Eustachian tube function and middle ear ventilation. Early detection of URTI, immunization, and control of environmental risk factors are needed to reduce the risk of AOM in children.

papers.title_original: The Relationship Between Upper Respiratory Tract Infections and the Incidence of Acute Otitis Media in Children: A Literature Review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates the relationship between upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) and the incidence of acute otitis media (AOM) in children, focusing on the role of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus as potential pathogens. The central question is whether URTI, particularly those caused by RSV and rhinovirus, increases the risk of AOM in children.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a literature analysis of 10 journals published between 2021 and 2025. It synthesizes findings to determine the association between URTI and AOM in children, including relevant risk factors and pathogens. The methodology involves reviewing and summarizing existing studies without conducting new experiments.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that URTI is associated with the occurrence of AOM in children through an inflammatory process that impairs Eustachian tube function and middle ear ventilation. It also identifies RSV and rhinovirus as particularly associated with AOM.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited to a literature review, and the findings are based on previously published studies. There is no mention of specific statistical methods or meta-analytic techniques used to consolidate the results. The review does not address the relative contributions of different pathogens or the mechanisms of inflammation in detail.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Early detection of URTI, immunization, and control of environmental risk factors are recommended to reduce the risk of AOM in children. Further research is needed to explore the specific roles of RSV and rhinovirus in AOM development and to identify effective interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the link between upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) and acute otitis media (AOM) in children, emphasizing the role of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus. It highlights that URTI can lead to inflammation and edema in the nasopharynx, impairing Eustachian tube function and increasing AOM risk. The review synthesizes findings from 10 studies published between 2021 and 2025, concluding that URTI is associated with AOM through inflammatory processes. It also notes that RSV and rhinovirus are particularly linked to AOM. The review suggests early detection of URTI, immunization, and environmental risk factor control as strategies to reduce AOM incidence. However, it lacks detailed statistical methods and does not explore the mechanisms of inflammation further. Future research should focus on the specific roles of RSV and rhinovirus in AOM development and on effective interventions.

papers.title: Advancing Vaccine Adjuvants: Regulatory Frameworks and Developmental Strategies
papers.abstract: Adjuvants have been an integral part of most vaccine formulations, mainly functioning as delivery systems and immunostimulants for antigens. Aluminum salts, the first adjuvants approved for human vaccine use, remain the most widely used adjuvants in EMA- and FDA-licensed vaccines. Adjuvants enhance vaccine-induced immune responses; improve vaccine efficacy, especially in populations vulnerable to infections such as the elderly and infants; provide antigen dose-sparing; and shape the immune profile of the vaccine-induced response. The effectiveness of vaccines is attributable primarily to the antigens as active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and the adjuvants as constituent material in the vaccine formulation. Adjuvants enhance vaccine effectiveness by activating the innate immune system and boosting adaptive immune responses to co-delivered antigens. Adjuvants function as immunostimulants or delivery systems, often acting as both by promoting antigen uptake by Antigen Presenting Cells (APCs) and triggering cytokine and chemokine release to improve B and T cell activation. Adjuvants are either endogenous, as found in live, attenuated, pathogen-based vaccines, or exogenous, added to, e.g., protein subunit or mRNA-based vaccines to boost immunogenicity. Over the past few decades, novel exogenous adjuvants have become critical to new vaccine development, serving both as delivery systems and immune stimulants. Notable examples include MF59, used in seasonal and pandemic influenza vaccines, and AS01, incorporated in shingles, malaria, and RSV vaccines. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated not only the development and use of mRNA vaccines adjuvanted by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) but also the development of novel adjuvants (e.g., Matrix M) and mimics (e.g., Advax-CpG) of those already present in licensed vaccines. While the growing interest in novel adjuvants has created new opportunities for development of vaccines and delivery systems, it has also introduced challenges in their development, regulation, and clinical application. The COVID-19 pandemic also exposed vulnerabilities in adjuvant availability and supply chains, underscoring the need for adjuvant mimics that can provide more accessible, scalable, and resilient alternatives. This paper explores the regulatory landscape surrounding the use of adjuvants in vaccines, highlighting critical aspects, opportunities and potential strategies for the development of novel adjuvants. It also addresses approaches to mitigate possible safety concerns and discusses the use of an adjuvant library established by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI).

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了 疫苗 佐剂的监管框架和开发策略。它重点关注佐剂在增强 疫苗 诱导的 呼吸道合胞病毒 中的作用,特别是对于 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和相关病原体。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对佐剂现有文献和监管指南的全面审查,包括佐剂作为免疫刺激剂或递送系统的功能。该研究还讨论了流行病防范创新联盟(CEPI)建立的佐剂库的使用。

Adjuvants are either endogenous, as found in live, attenuated, pathogen-based vaccines, or exogenous, added to, e.g., protein subunit or mRNA-based vaccines to boost immunogenicity. Over the past few decades, novel exogenous adjuvants have become critical to new vaccine development, serving both as delivery systems and immune stimulants. Notable examples include MF59, used in seasonal and pandemic influenza vaccines, and AS01, incorporated in shingles, malaria, and RSV vaccines. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated not only the development and use of mRNA vaccines adjuvanted by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) but also the development of novel adjuvants (e.g., Matrix M) and mimics (e.g., Advax-CpG) of those already present in licensed vaccines. While the growing interest in novel adjuvants has created new opportunities for development of vaccines and delivery systems, it has also introduced challenges in their development, regulation, and clinical application. The COVID-19 pandemic also exposed vulnerabilities in adjuvant availability and supply chains, underscoring the need for adjuvant mimics that can provide more accessible, scalable, and resilient alternatives. This paper explores the regulatory landscape surrounding the use of adjuvants in vaccines, highlighting critical aspects, opportunities and potential strategies for the development of novel adjuvants. It also addresses approaches to mitigate possible safety concerns and discusses the use of an adjuvant library established by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI).

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 佐剂是大多数 疫苗 制剂的组成部分,主要用作抗原的递送系统和免疫刺激剂。该研究解决了对先进 疫苗 佐剂的需求,特别是在 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 及其相关挑战的背景下。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了 疫苗 佐剂的监管框架和开发策略。它重点关注佐剂在增强 疫苗 诱导的 呼吸道合胞病毒 中的作用,特别是对于 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和相关病原体。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对佐剂现有文献和监管指南的全面审查,包括佐剂作为免疫刺激剂或递送系统的功能。该研究还讨论了流行病防范创新联盟(CEPI)建立的佐剂库的使用。
analysis_zh.main_results: 疫苗 的有效性主要归因于作为活性药物成分(API)的抗原和作为 疫苗 制剂中的组成材料的佐剂。佐剂通过激活先天免疫系统并增强 免疫应答 对共递送抗原的适应性来增强 疫苗 的有效性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 人们对新型佐剂日益增长的兴趣为疫苗和递送系统的开发创造了新的机遇,但也给它们的开发、监管和临床应用带来了挑战。本文探讨了 疫苗 中佐剂使用的监管环境,重点介绍了新型佐剂开发的关键方面、机遇和潜在策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更容易获得、可扩展和有弹性的佐剂提供信息,特别是针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和其他相关病原体。该研究还提出了减轻与佐剂相关的可能安全问题的方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告与研究相关的具体局限性或证据强度。基于对佐剂及其在 疫苗 开发中的作用的一般讨论,信心是中等的。

papers.full_text: INTRODUCTION eview question / Objective Objective: to inform a risk-based approach to eye protection (goggles, face shields and visors) against respiratory disease transmission in healthcare workers, taking account of causal mechanisms. Questions: 1. Does eye protection reduce respiratory infection i n h e a l t h c a r e w o r k e r s , a n d i n w h i c h circumstances? 2. What do the mechanisms of disease and of the intervention predict about the size of any effect, for different pathogens and exposure scenarios? 3. What can the existing studies show, given their designs, biases and power, and how have their findings been interpreted in later reviews and guidance? Rationale Eye protection is recommended for healthcare workers against several respiratory pathogens, and universal eye protection was widely adopted during the COVID-19 pandemic. The evidence usually cited is observational and has been summarised in earlier reviews, some of which pooled crude estimates and paid limited attention to bias. Eye protection is rarely worn on its own: it aligns with masks, respirators, gowns and gloves, so associations with infection may reflect the whole protective ensemble or the careful worker rather than the eyewear specifically. The role of the eye also differs by pathogen. For some viruses, such as adenovirus and H7 avian influenza, the eye is a site of active infection. For others it is at most an entry route. A new review, which interprets each study against these mechanisms, is needed to establish what the evidence can and cannot show. INPLASY ￼1 International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols INPLASY Efficacy of eye protection in reducing respiratory disease transmission in healthcare workers: a mechanism-informed narrative synthesis Greenhalgh, T; Oliver, M; Atan, D; Helm, R; Kanou, L. ADMINISTRATIVE INFORMATION Support - UKRI Cross Research Council Responsive Mode (CRCRM) grant 25130 for Interdisciplinary Research to Jon Williamson (University of Manchester), Trisha Greenhalgh (University of Oxford) and Rebecca Helm (UCL). The funder had no role in developing the protocol or the conduct of the study. Review stage at the time of initial registration - Data analysis. Conflicts of interest - None declared. INPLASY registration number: INPLASY2026110068 Amendments - This protocol was registered with the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (INPLASY) on 19 November 2026 and was last updated on 19 November 2026.
